Name: PAVE Space
Description:
PAVE Space is a Swiss company built on the success of the Gruyère Space Program, which developed Europe’s first reusable rocket demonstrator.

Its expertise spans space propulsion, control algorithms, and rapid integration of complex systems.

PAVE Space now targets last-mile satellite delivery, using its kickstage to move multi-ton payloads from low Earth orbit to any orbit within 24 hours.

Name: Space4Impact
Description:
We believe that Space can do more for Earth.

@Space4Impact we promote the adoption of space technologies that have a positive impact on Earth. As part of our Space2Earth Accelerator, we help space startups to bring the power of satellite data to new markets.

Name: European Space Deep-Tech Innovation Centre (ESDI)
Description:
The European Space Deep-tech Innovation Centre (ESDI) is a collaborative initiative between the European Space Agency (ESA) and Switzerland, established to accelerate the commercial adoption and availability of deep-tech for the benefit of ESA, its Member States, and the broader European space sector.

Starting with the ESA Phi-Lab Switzerland, ESDI designs, establishes and runs platforms for deep-tech research in quantum, data, and materials, bringing to use technologies of tomorrow for the world of today.

Name: Space Systems Innovation Platform - SSIP
Description:
Breaking barriers and building bridges beyond borders.

SSIP is an independent Swiss ecosystem platform based at Technopark Luzern, dedicated to accelerating collaboration between academia, industry, research centers, and global partners in the fields of space, microgravity, and advanced industrial innovation.

Originally initiated through the NASA Space Apps Challenge Lucerne, SSIP has evolved into a high-impact platform focused on translating research and technological capabilities into industrial and commercial reality through pilot programs, industry forums, innovation challenges, and long-term strategic partnerships.

Our mission is to strengthen Swiss technological leadership while building global value chains that enable sustainable growth, industrial competitiveness, and cross-sector collaboration.

From Switzerland to the world, SSIP connects innovators, engineers, entrepreneurs, researchers, and institutions to co-create next-generation solutions in space, life sciences, and advanced manufacturing.

Focus areas:
• Microgravity-enabled Research, Biotech & Biomanufacturing
• Space Systems, In-Orbit Platforms & Earth Observation
• Advanced & Additive Manufacturing for Space and Life Sciences
• AI-Native Research, Robotics & Automation
• Dual-Use Industrial Technologies and System Integration
• Education, Innovation & Talent Development

 Join us - collaborate, innovate, and help shape Europe’s next industrial frontier in space and microgravity.

Name: Stellar Alpina
Description:
Stellar Alpina is a Zurich-based space venture developing high-performance Rotating Detonation Engines, modular in-space vehicles and lunar delivery systems. Our mission is to build upstream hardware that gives Europe a sovereign path to the Moon.

Founded by ARIS Alumni, we combine hands-on engine development, system design expertise and shared leadership to create a scalable architecture for propulsion and lunar access.

Our work is grounded in Swiss precision and driven by the belief that world-class space systems can be built in Zurich.

Stellar Alpina is shaping the next chapter of European space infrastructure: engines, vehicles and landers built to deliver reliably to the lunar surface.

Name: Space Sustainability Rating
Description:
The Space Sustainability Rating (SSR) is a voluntary rating system providing space actors with a transparent rating and certification system to assess the level of #sustainability of their missions. 

It also offers practical guidance on how to improve missions’ sustainability performance, with the goal of helping to address the challenges raised by the proliferation of space debris. 

Developed in the last three years by a consortium including the World Economic Forum, the European Space Agency, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, BryceTech and the University of Texas at Austin, the rating provides an innovative solution for space operators to support their debris mitigation efforts and increase the sustainability of their missions. 

All space actors are welcomed to join the SSR. If you wish to learn more about the rating and explore opportunities for engagement please visit our website.

Name: Chair of Space Geodesy, ETH Zurich
Description:
The Chair of Space Geodesy will face the challenges and profit from the opportunities that come with “big data” in geodesy. We will design and implement advanced machine learning techniques to automate the processing of GNSS and VLBI data, resulting in a faster availability and higher quality of geodetic products. Also, machine learning will be applied in the large-scale analysis of GNSS time series to detect and investigate geophysical signals, inter alia related to hydrological and seismic events, as well as to severe weather events and ionospheric disturbances. Finally, we aim to improve the prediction of several types of geodetic parameters by machine learning. In particular, we will focus on determining future Earth orientation parameters, station coordinates and atmospheric parameters.

Prof. Dr. Benedikt Soja

Name: gamma.earth
Description: Uniquely powerful AI solutions for Earth Observation and remote sensing. 10x super-resolution for multispectral and hyperspectral satellite imaging data. Cloud detection and removal, atmospheric correction, as well as land use and land cover classification.

Name: Swiss Hackathon | Orbital Infrastructure Challenge
Description:
Swiss Hackathon is a national Swiss innovation initiative bringing together engineers, researchers, entrepreneurs, AI specialists, biotech innovators, cybersecurity experts, advanced manufacturing professionals and space industry stakeholders to solve some of the most important challenges shaping the future of the orbital economy.

Through the Orbital Infrastructure Challenge, participants collaborate across six strategic domains:

 Orbital Digital Twins
 Artificial Intelligence
 Biotech & Pharma in Microgravity
 Advanced Manufacturing & Future Materials
 Space Cybersecurity & Resilience
 Digital Twin Earth Switzerland

More than a traditional hackathon, Swiss Hackathon is a platform designed to connect industry, academia, research institutions and emerging talent around real-world challenges with real deployment potential.

Our mission is to accelerate innovation, foster collaboration and help transform ideas into pilots, products, companies and future infrastructure.

We welcome sponsors, industrial partners, universities, research institutions, technology companies, mentors and innovators who want to help shape the next generation of Swiss and global technological leadership.

 Orbital Infrastructure Challenge 2026
 Lucerne, Switzerland
 3–5 October 2026

Powered by SSIP × TECHNOPARK Luzern × HSLU

Name: LIFE Space Mission
Description:
We are LIFE, a Swiss-led and European-driven space mission dedicated to answer one of humanity’s oldest and most profound questions: Are we alone?

Our goal is simple but bold — to build the first mission designed solely to detect signs of life on planets beyond our Solar System. Using mid-infrared interferometry, we study the atmospheres of distant worlds, searching for chemical fingerprints that might reveal biological activity. Building on Switzerland’s pioneering legacy in exoplanet science, LIFE continues to lead the way in exploring new worlds.

But we’re more than a scientific mission. We’re a team of scientists, engineers, and communicators united by curiosity and purpose. For us, space exploration goes beyond science — it’s a shared journey that brings people together and inspires new ways of thinking.
We challenge conventions, embrace complexity, and explore new ways of working together. By reimagining how space missions are built, we want to show that openness, creativity, and collaboration can move science forward — and inspire the next generation to think bigger.

We’re just getting started — so stay tuned

Name: CFS Engineering
Description:
CFS Engineering is a consultancy company founded in August 1999, located in the Business Park (PSE) of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (EPFL) in Lausanne, Switzerland.
The mission of CFS Engineering is:

To offer services in the Numerical Simulation of Fluid Mechanics and Structural Mechanics Engineering Problems

Numerical simulation of complex engineering problems is becoming increasingly important in product design, but requires highly specialized knowledge and tools. CFS Engineering has this knowledge and the tools to work with its customers to better understand the physics of complex engineering problems, with the ultimate goal of improving product design and/or performance.

CFS Engineering is a Societe Anonyme (SA) with 3 share holders, RUAG Aerospace, Silvio Merazzi, and Jan B. Vos.

Name: Build a CubeSat
Description: I am developing a relatively affordable, open source CubeSat project and documenting my progress on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@buildacubesat

Name: Center for Space and Habitability (CSH), University of Bern
Description: The mission of the Center for Space and Habitability (CSH) is to foster dialogue and interactions between the various scientific disciplines interested in the formation, detection and characterisation of other worlds within and beyond the Solar System, our search for life elsewhere in the Universe, and its implications for disciplines outside of the sciences. Our members, affiliates and collaborators include astronomers, astrophysicists and astrochemists, atmospheric, climate and planetary scientists, geologists and geophysicists, biochemists and philosophers. We are home to the CSH and Bernoulli Fellowships, which host young, dynamic and talented researchers from all over the world to conduct independent research. We actively run a series of programs to stimulate interdisciplinary research within the University of Bern, Switzerland, including collaborations and/or open dialogue with Medicine and Philosophy. We are active in scientific mediation and outreach activities with the general public and in promoting equality, diversity and inclusion in science.

Name: ESMATS | European Space Mechanisms and Tribology Symposium
Description:
Since its inception in 1983 ESMATS has come to be recognised as the premier vehicle for Mechanisms Engineers, experienced and new recruits, to come together to discuss and celebrate their successes and failures, with a view to pooling their knowledge for the betterment of this unique community and the European Space industry as a whole.

ESMATS is held bi-annually, alternating in collaboration with its sister event in the USA - The Aerospace Mechanisms Symposium.

The European Space Mechanisms and Tribology Symposium, ESMATS, regularly attracts more than 250 space mechanism designers and engineers, space scientists, satellite project and programme managers from around the world.

Name: SpaceHopper
Description:
A hopping robot for asteroid exploration.

In the SpaceHopper project, students at ETH Zurich developed a robot capable of moving in low gravity environments through hopping motions. It is intended to be used in future space missions to explore small celestial bodies. The exploration of asteroids and moons could provide insights into the formation of the universe and they may contain valuable minerals that humanity could use in the future.

The project began in 2021 as an ETH focusproject for bachelor's students. Now, it is being continued as a regular research project. A particular challenge in developing exploration robots for asteroids is that, unlike larger celestial bodies like Earth, there is low gravity on asteroids and moons. The students have therefore tested their robot's functionality in zero gravity during a parabolic flight. The parabolic flight was conducted in collaboration with the European Space Agency as part of the ESA Academy Experiments Programme.

Name: Space Campus
Description:
Founded in 2023 on the shores of Lake Léman (Switzerland), Space Campus is an initiative launched by the Swiss Armed Forces Space Command. Based in Lausanne (VD), Space Campus connects young professionals with technical and military backgrounds, to projects revolving around defense and space.

Our core activities lie in the realm of: Space Situational Awareness, Information Research & Intelligence Gathering (IMINT/SIGINT), Robust SATCOM, Precise Navigation, Countermeasures, and Prototypes.

The Swiss Space Command wants to accelerate the contribution of young talents in the research & development of technologies and capabilities having a direct use by the Swiss Armed Forces and armasuisse. Space Campus creates the link between the Swiss space industry and universities, through academic and industrial projects developed by young professionals (BSc, MSc, PhD).

Name: Lepto GmbH
Description:
Lepto is a deep-tech spin-off from Empa, developing ultrathin, energy-efficient, and ultra-light terahertz (THz) photonic devices. Our technology enables the next generation of space and telecommunications systems, bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and real-world applications.
We design and manufacture THz optical components such as filters, polarizers, and gratings, with a growing pipeline of advanced devices tailored for satellite–Earth communications, Earth observation instruments, and 6G networks.
Beyond our hardware solutions, we also provide consulting in advanced photonics and terahertz technologies, supporting partners in the aerospace, telecom, and research sectors.
At Lepto, our mission is to make THz radiation accessible, scalable, and impactful, accelerating innovation in secure communications, space exploration, and beyond.

Name: Spacetalk
Description: Spacetalk ensures the viability of Outer Space activities by providing a collaborative communication platform where all space actors worldwide can share their orbital data.

Name: Space Eye - Observatorium für Weltraum und Umwelt
Description:
Das Space Eye - Observatorium für Weltraum und Umwelt ist ein Besuchs- und Bildungszentrum und fördert das Bewusstsein über die Erde, ihrer Umgebung im Universum und die Bedeutung der MINT-Wissenschaften.

Wir bringen Menschen mit der Faszination für den Weltraum und die Naturwissenschaften zusammen mit den führenden Organisationen der Forschung, Bildung und Technologie. Durch Bewusstwerdung für das Wunder des Lebens überhaupt, den Fragen nach dem woher wir kommen und wohin wir gehen, werden auch philosophische Aspekte unseres Daseins auf der Erde geweckt.

Name: PIKALI Réunion & Suisse
Description:
PIKALI RUN OI est une association née à La Réunion, engagée dans la promotion du spatial, des sciences, de l’innovation et de l’égalité des chances.

À travers des ateliers, conférences, événements, actions scolaires et projets de coopération, PIKALI rend le spatial plus accessible aux jeunes, aux territoires ultramarins et au grand public.

L’association s’inscrit aujourd’hui dans la dynamique du réseau VELIO SPACE, aux côtés d’initiatives comme PIKALI Suisse et PIKALI France Académique, afin de créer des passerelles entre La Réunion, la Guyane, les Antilles, l’Europe, la Suisse, l’Afrique et l’international.

Nos priorités : éducation spatiale, métiers de demain, inclusion, développement durable, applications du spatial pour l’air, la terre et la mer, et coopération entre territoires.

Notre conviction : le spatial est un levier d’éducation, d’inspiration et de transformation.

Réyoné Nou Lé Kapab.

Name: SQAT project
Description:
SQAT is a 3.5-year project, funded under the Horizon Europe Programme, that focuses on Implementing Smart Farming Applications using EO Data, Soil Sensors & Robotics.

SQAT's smart soil mapping service is a multi-level, multi-technology and multi-purpose solution. With a keen eye on markets and users, SQAT’s approach is designed to overcome today’s practical, technical and financial challenges to generate high resolution soil properties maps and demand-driven products like application maps for soil improvement or crop management, or compliancy proof for eco schemes. Our vision is that the integration of different technologies provides a flexible and agile service beating the unbundled alternatives that are now in the market: our in-situ sampling and/or sensoring is wrapped in a Copernicus-based artificial intelligence soil mapping product.

Name: CHiwi Foundation
Description:
The CHiwi Foundation is a nonprofit organisation dedicated to encouraging research, education, and innovation in advanced mathematics, alternative energy, and space exploration.

Our goal is to support high-impact scientific research and make it possible for scholars and researchers all around the world to continue making significant strides in these fields.

The Foundation carries out its mission by awarding grants to research projects in space exploration, alternative energy, and advanced mathematics.

Both individuals and organisations can submit grant applications, and they can do so from anywhere in the world. We operate both in Switzerland and abroad.

Name: AD ASTRA Space Architecture

AD ASTRA | Space Architecture
At AD ASTRA, we design the future of human life beyond Earth. From interstellar vessels like Project Hyperion to large-scale orbital systems such as the Sunshades Project, our work merges architecture, astrophysics, and engineering to create sustainable habitats and ecosystems in space. We engineer modular living systems, artificial gravity environments, and self-sustaining agriculture, enabling civilizations to thrive off-world. As both a space innovation lab and think tank, AD ASTRA shapes the architecture of tomorrow-on Earth and among the stars.

Name: Origine Labs
Description:
Origine Labs is an independent engineering studio building scientific instruments and advanced technology from first principles.
We design, prototype, and validate systems across optics, astronomy instrumentation, embedded electronics, and applied physics — bridging theory with real-world hardware. Our work combines rigorous science, clean engineering, and an obsession for precision.

Science, Engineered.

Origine Labs — Astrotechnica

Astrotechnica is the astronomy and optics division of Origine Labs, focused on scientific instruments for astronomy, optics, and adaptive optics. We document the full engineering journey — from theoretical models and system design to prototyping, measurement, validation, and iteration.

Origine Labs also explores related technical fields including radio astronomy, microwave engineering, signal processing, mathematics, cryptography, and open-source intelligence.

Origine Labs is a civilian R&D initiative and does not engage in military or defense activities.

Name: SE2S GmbH
Description:
SE2S GmbH is a cutting-edge Swiss company specializing in radiation qualification, particle detection, and data analysis. Established in 2020 by a team of radiation qualification and testing experts, electronics designers, hardware and software developers, and aerospace data evaluation specialists, SE2S offers state-of-the-art products and services.

As a spin-off of the Paul Scherrer Institute, SE2S GmbH excels in radiation detection systems, utilizing advanced technologies and cutting-edge electronics. Their innovative detector technologies are specifically designed to thrive in diverse radiation environments, particularly in aerospace applications. The company also develops ground support equipment and software to facilitate radiation detection.

SE2S GmbH provides a comprehensive range of radiation qualification and testing services. Their extensive offerings include radiation testing, detector calibration, and the development of systems and electronics for radiation qualification. They possess extensive expertise in radiation hardness assurance, ensuring the durability and resilience of their products.

In addition to their hardware solutions, SE2S GmbH offers radiation analysis software and services. Their proficiency lies in space environment and radiation modeling, enabling them to accurately calculate and simulate radiation environments. They are also highly skilled in assessing the effects of radiation on electronics.

By combining their proficiency in radiation qualification, particle detection, and data analysis, SE2S GmbH delivers innovative solutions that effectively tackle the complex challenges of the high-tech industry.

Name: PEROSPACE
Description: PEROSPACE is a deep-tech startup pioneering new generation photovoltaic (PV) technology for space applications. PEROSPACE’s technology offers lightweight, high-performance photovoltaic solutions with 80% cost advantage and high-volume, scalable production, which are critical for the growing constellation-based space economy. Our ambition is to introduce a transformative "new space" approach by providing highly efficient, accessible, and scalable PV solutions.

Name: Space Data Centers
Description:
Overcoming RF bandwidth and latency limitations of existing "every satellite has it's own downlink" scenarios requires radically new solutions. Among others: Aggregating data at the edge, i.e. in space, creating actionable insights at the edge, i.e. yet again in space, high-speed point-to-point networks between aggregation points, i.e. space data centres, distributed workload management, artificial intelligence, hardware- and software acceleration of workloads and networks etc.
In this project we derive, study and benchmark different space data centre architectures for selected use-cases, from user-requirements down to the hardware and software stack and the network architecture. 
We are building a publicly available tool for everyone to play with, select key-technologies, configurations, scale and system architectures to, as objectively as possible, compare different scenarios.
We are excited to have assembled a highly interdisciplinary team from KP Labs and IBM bringing together expertise ranging from AI/ML, hardware, software, data centre design and operation, networking, security, space craft integration, edge computing software & hardware, etc.
On top of that, key stakeholders from the space industry are building our backbone on our advisory board.
If you would like to get involved in any way, don't hesitate to reach out to us by direct contact or leave us a post.

Name: Space Biostasis Coalition
Description:
SBC is a Swiss-US research association. As a non-profit, SBC operates as a neutral convening ground for scientists, engineers, inventors, entrepreneurs, policymakers, and corporations, accelerating progress toward shared technological breakthroughs that benefit humanity’s efforts in the exploration and industrialization of space. 

SBC doesn't claim ownership of discoveries. Scientists retain full rights to their innovations while gaining access to unprecedented funding pools and cross-industry expertise. Space companies can collaborate without fear of losing competitive advantage.

Mission 
The Space Biostasis Coalition accelerates the development of human biostasis technologies for space exploration by uniting researchers, industry leaders, and policymakers to unlock $1 billion in frontier biostasis research funding, advance scientific knowledge, and inspire global collaboration toward humanity's sustainable expansion beyond Earth.

SBC catalyzes breakthrough advances in human biostasis research by:
- Building strategic alliances between space companies and biostasis researchers
- Publishing authoritative scientific resources that define the state of the art
- Mobilizing $1 billion in public and private funding for frontier biostasis R&D
- Hosting world-class scientific conferences and advocating for incentive prizes in the field
- Inspiring public engagement through compelling narratives about humanity's future

Vision 
We envision a future where breakthrough biostasis technologies enable safe, long-duration human space travel, transforming humanity into a thriving multiplanetary species while advancing medical science and preservation capabilities that benefit all life on Earth and beyond.
